answer: Latency triangulation ties each identity to one network place. Independent landmarks send unpredictable ping challenges, and the identity must reply with round-trip times consistent with a single physical location. One machine fronting many accounts cannot sit at the nadir of latency to distant landmarks at once, so the triangle of measurements exposes the shared route. Each extra fake identity needs its own presence, with its own link and address, and that cost cannot be shared. A walnut in one drawer and an ivory claim of location prove nothing; only latency measured from many sides does.
